I couldn’t decide at first:
MSFS 2020 — fully patched, working avionics, VR support, tons of DLC, Deluxe + Premium for around $40  
vs.
MSFS 2024 — unpolished, still work in progress, no real content yet.

Man, I’m so glad I grabbed 2020.
Fantastic visuals, easy‑mode flying around locations we know, and suddenly 14 hours were gone, especially with the Oculus Rift.
4070 Super — everything runs perfectly.

But beware of the content size:
The installation with almost everything is around 180 GB, and there are another 220 GB you can download.
So keep a lot of space free — you really have to commit.
Steam only downloads the small client (~2 GB), but Microsoft downloads the full package, and it counts as playtime.
If you already have a Microsoft account, there’s no fuss at all.

I’m absolutely flashed — the whole experience was worth it.
I already got my money’s worth after 16 hours, and there’s more to come.
Fantastic stuff, especially the Maverick missions, the Dune content, and tons of aircraft.

I just flew the F‑18 Hornet for about 4 hours, visited different locations, got a bit dizzy, took tons of screenshots, and then took a well‑earned break.
I’m going to dream about it tonight.
It’s the best thing that has happened to me in gaming for years.

VR, triple monitor, single monitor — everything works.
I’m playing with an old Saitek keyboard and mouse, and I’m even going to use my GT wheel pedals as rudder pedals.
Having a blast 😄
UL, PPL or LAPL — I’m coming!  

2020 is a 10 out of 10.
I’d absolutely recommend Premium Deluxe for $40 and wait until 2024 is properly patched and polished. 😄
Until then, I’ve got more than enough to enjoy — especially with tons of forums, mods, and ongoing support still available.
The flow and visuals are fantastic on an i5‑12600K and a 4070 Super.
(Assign controls to the axis only — no jitter at all.)
First time I passed on being an early adopter — and it was absolutely worth the money spent

My favorite thing is the graphics since when you got max settings it looks so realistic.
Also when they say you can fly anywhere, you can fly anywhere, its truly amazing being able to visit your house in any video game.

Microsoft Flight Simulator 2020 represents a monumental achievement in digital aviation, delivering a replication of global flight that emphasizes photorealism. By leveraging cloud-based geospatial data and real-time weather tracking, the simulation captures the grandeur of atmospheric navigation. The flight dynamics are sophisticated, translating complex aerodynamic forces and air density into a tangible sense of flight that rewards precision. The staggering scale of the world is complemented by meticulous audio design, from the distinct hum of a single-engine propeller to the roar of a commercial turbofan. A thriving add-on ecosystem allows for the customization of hangars with detailed aircraft and bespoke scenery, transforming the title into a personalized aviation sandbox for both casual sightseers and pilots.

1: this game was the thing that got me to love aviation so much and its to this day one of my favorite hobbies.
2: i bought this game in 2023 (i think at least im not sure), and to be honest even now in 2026 i love to play this a lot as its really stable for me (i dont have msfs 2024 nor am i planning to buy it).

claims.claim: Reviewers experience lengthy download times and issues with the game's installation manager and launcher.

citations.review_text:
This game helps a ton if you're looking to familiarize yourself with instruments and how careful you gotta be in an aircraft. I would recommend it but this game requires you to have it running for a download of over 125+gbs in Microsoft's own launcher. Even with high-speed internet the download speed is capped and it can take over two hours just to start playing, putting you over the refund window.
If i had cared more back when i first bought this years ago, i would've found an alternative not related to this company. 
Also, you have to pay full price for the Deluxe edition even if you have Standard. and when uninstalling this I figured out that you have to manually delete the files in AppData due to the in-game launcher.

If anyone reading this decides to get the game, it runs pretty smoothly on a laptop with the attached specs. It helped me familiarize myself with the instruments of a SMALL aircraft before i scheduled a discovery flight, but it is not enough experience to fly anything. just interactive basics. Aside from that this game has some fun stuff like Landing Challenges with point-based completion ranks that i enjoyed.
LONG ASS INSTALLATION MANAGER 55 HOURS AND STILL 10 PRECENT

I would recommend it but this game requires you to have it running for a download of over 125+gbs in Microsoft's own launcher. Even with high-speed internet the download speed is capped and it can take over two hours just to start playing, putting you over the refund window.
